_note: Recorded from the backend (GET /api/methods/tlds, GET /api/methods/rule-drift and GET /api/sources/notifications on the repository's monitoring ledger, 2026-10-20).

method.formula: D = 100 × (w_T·T + w_S·S + w_L·L + w_R·R), every component in [0, 1]
method.weights_status: Chosen by the project as provisional research parameters before evaluation. They were not learned from data, not optimised and not legally validated.

textual.measures: How many words were inserted, deleted or substituted, per word of the longer clause.
textual.why_this_weight: 0.20: a surface measure. One changed word can reverse a duty, so it is kept well below legal effect; S measures similar wording, so T is not given more.

semantic.measures: How far the two clauses' word-hash vectors moved apart (1 − cosine). It is a word-overlap stand-in, not a pretrained meaning model.
semantic.why_this_weight: 0.30: the weight intended for meaning-level change. Because the current vector reflects shared words, T and S together give surface wording 0.50 of the score.

legal_effect.measures: The most severe change found in the rule fields (duty, penalty, amount or limit, deadline, exception, scope, person, action), on a 0–1 rubric.
legal_effect.why_this_weight: 0.40: closest to the research question about legally applicable change, so the largest single weight; kept below 0.50 so no single component decides the score alone.

rule_structure.measures: The share of the clause's rule elements that were inserted, deleted or substituted.
rule_structure.why_this_weight: 0.10: a coarse count that repeats some of what legal effect sees, so it gets the least weight.

method.bands_note: Provisional lower bounds applied to the score rounded to one decimal; not empirically validated.
method.missing: A component that cannot be computed is null with a reason, never 0. The score is COMPLETE only when all four exist; otherwise INCOMPLETE with value null and a separately named partial_value = 100 × Σ_available w_i·x_i ÷ Σ_available w_i that must not be compared with complete scores.
method.note: An indicator of change between two versions of one clause, not the percentage of a statute that changed, not legal correctness, not a probability, not materiality and not risk. Read legal-effect drift beside it: a small wording change can carry a large legal effect.

sensitivity.finding: On 59 held-out changes with a complete score, the default weights put 42 changes with a material legal effect (0.5 or more) in the Low band. Other weightings move many changes between bands while barely changing their order, so the band depends on the weight choice. There are no expert labels to say which weighting is right.

rule_method.score: sum of the weights of fields whose operation is ADDED, REMOVED or CHANGED (0-100). Fields marked UNCERTAIN are excluded and reported; the score is then a lower bound.

fields.label: Duty, permission or prohibition
fields.why: changes whether conduct is required, allowed or forbidden, the core of a legal instruction

fields.label: Penalty
fields.why: changes the consequence of non-compliance; an amount inside a penalty counts here only, never twice

fields.label: Amount or numeric limit
fields.why: changes when the rule bites, how much is at stake, or how many are allowed

fields.label: Exception or proviso
fields.why: changes who or what escapes the rule

fields.label: Scope (what the rule covers)
fields.why: changes what or whom the rule covers

fields.label: Person or body named
fields.why: changes who acts, approves or is bound (low weight: the extractor is a heuristic)

fields.label: What must be done
fields.why: changes what must be done (low weight: the extractor is a heuristic)

rationale.status: Provisional research-design choices, stated when rule drift was introduced (docs/methodology/legal_change_fingerprint.v1.md): the weights rank legal function. They were not learned from data, not optimised and not reviewed or approved by a legal expert. The tier order is the stated reasoning; the exact numbers inside that order are this project's choice.
rationale.total: The eight weights add up to 100, so a score reads as the share of the fields' combined weight that changed: 100 would mean every field changed. It is not a percentage of legal importance.

tiers.reason: Whether conduct is required, allowed or forbidden is the core of a legal instruction; changing it changes the kind of rule, so it gets the highest weight.
The consequence of breaking the rule, when it applies (amounts and numeric limits) and when compliance is due. Each changes what a person must do or risks without changing the kind of instruction.
Who or what the rule covers or exempts. These matter, but the core instruction stays in place.
Who acts and what must be done also matter legally, but they are detected with a phrase list and a verb list. A low weight limits the effect of those heuristic detections being wrong.

rationale.counting: A field adds its weight once when it is added, removed or changed, however many words changed inside it. A field the extractor marks uncertain adds nothing and is listed, so the score is then a lower bound. A change outside every field is Not scored, never 0.
rationale.not_the_combined_weights: These are the rule-drift field weights (a 0–100 rule score). They are separate from the 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.1 weights of the combined indicator (TLDS), which combine four different measures.

sensitivity.finding: Tiered alternatives keep the order of rule scores (Spearman 0.952 or more against the current weights; at least 99.9% of strictly ordered pairs keep their order under every alternative). Removing the tiers (equal weights) mostly changes ties: 614 pairs switch between tied and ordered (Spearman 0.812). So the tier structure, more than the exact numbers, decides which changes score alike. The most often changed field is actor (31 of 59 changes); actor and action are the heuristic fields, so their low weight limits how much extraction errors move the scores.
sensitivity.note: No expert labels exist, so no weighting is shown to be more correct; this checks stability only. Legal validation: UNVERIFIED.
